rationale: Two major findings block merge: (1) all three commit subjects use a lowercase first word and will fail Tekton CI commit-format validation; (2) NavigationMore combines refs with an inline arrow function that creates a new callback on every render, causing floating-ui to tear down and re-set its reference element each cycle — the idiomatic fix is useMergeRefs from @floating-ui/react. All seven acceptance criteria are met; lenses ran fully; no security or breaking-change risk.

useFocusReturn unit tests: all four cases present and correct
NavigationMore: triggerRef + useFocusReturn + combined ref callback
NavigationMore test: open → Escape → trigger has focus

standards_review.notes: All three commits use a lowercase first word after the colon: 'add useFocusReturn hook', 'return focus to trigger on NavigationMore close', 'return focus to trigger on SearchableCombobox close'. The guide requires EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence (first word uppercase). Tekton CI enforces this regex and will block the MR. Correct forms: 'Add useFocusReturn hook', 'Return focus to trigger on NavigationMore close', 'Return focus to trigger on SearchableCombobox close'.
No untrusted input rendered, no new API surface, no secrets introduced.

NavigationMore uses an inline arrow function as a dual-assignment callback ref: (el) => { triggerRef.current = el; refs.setReference(el) }. This creates a new function identity on every render, causing React to call the old ref with null then the new with el on each cycle, triggering unnecessary floating-ui reference teardown/setup. The @floating-ui/react package exports useMergeRefs for exactly this purpose.

findings.problem: All three commit subjects begin with a lowercase word, violating the project's enforced commit format (EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence).
findings.impact: Tekton CI will block the MR with a commit-format failure before any reviewer sees it.
findings.recommendation: Reword via interactive rebase: 'Add useFocusReturn hook', 'Return focus to trigger on NavigationMore close', 'Return focus to trigger on SearchableCombobox close'.

findings.problem: The trigger button uses an inline arrow function `(el) => { triggerRef.current = el; refs.setReference(el) }` to combine two refs. React creates a new function object on every render, so it calls the old ref with null then the new ref with the element each cycle, causing @floating-ui/react to reset its reference element state on every render.
findings.impact: Unnecessary floating-ui lifecycle calls and potential positioning micro-jitter on every NavigationMore re-render. Violates floating-ui's recommended stable-ref contract; could manifest as visible flicker in future library versions.
findings.recommendation: Import useMergeRefs from @floating-ui/react: `const mergedRef = useMergeRefs([triggerRef, refs.setReference])`, then use `ref={mergedRef}` on the button. useMergeRefs returns a memoized stable callback that only fires on actual mount/unmount.
